[[LINE08]] #Step 2: Call the function [[LINE09]] values_1 = [2.0, 11, 4, 5, 3, 3.5, 4, 10, 16] [[LINE10]] values_2 = [7, 11, 3] [[LINE11]] search_lists(values_1, values_2) [[LINE-EXPLANATIONS]] [[LINE02.EXPL1]] We need to first declare the function so that we can call it later. The following lines declare the function search_lists that takes two lists and prints the elements in the 2nd list (the list referred by variable lst2) that exist in the 1st list (the list referred by variable lst1).

Note that all statements following the header line are indented. [[LINE04.EXPL1]] We want to iterate over the list lst2 and check whether each element of the 2nd list exists in the 1st list. We iterate through the values in the 2nd list using for loop because for loop can step across any kind of sequence object including lists. [[LINE04.EXPL2]] This for loop assigns the name val2 to each of the values in the list lst2 in turn, from left to right, and then the statements in the loop body will be executed for each. [[LINE04.EXPL3]] Note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header. [[LINE06.EXPL1]] To determine if the visited value in the 2nd list exists in the 1st list, we employ the in operator to test membership. Because the in operator implicitly scans the list looking for a match. [[LINE06.EXPL2]] If the visited value in the 2nd list (val2) exists in the 1st list, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped. [[LINE07.EXPL1]] This statement prints to the default standard output stream the value in the 2nd list that exists in the 1st list followed by the text "exists in both list".
The printed text shows the arguments of the print function separated by the default delimiter (i.e., single space character) and followed by the end-of-line character at the end. [[LINE09.EXPL1]] We define list referred by variable values_1 to hold the values in the 1st list. We initialize the list by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in square brackets [ ]. [[LINE10.EXPL1]] We define list referred by variable values_2 to hold the values in the 2nd list. We initialize the list by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in square brackets [ ]. [[LINE11.EXPL1]] This statement calls the search_lists function and passes the 1st and 2nd list as its arguments. Note that the function call must be done after the function is declared.
